video_title: Could the Mavs select one of Dusty May’s Michigan players at No. 9? | NBA Draft Preview

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Mavericks hire Dusty May after firing Jason Kidd
quotes.excerpt: Nico Harrison to run this organization, fire Jason Kidd within weeks after bringing in Masai Ujiri.
quotes.quote: Think back to the last eight months. Patrick Dumont, the Mavericks owner, you let go of Nico Harrison and then bring in Masai Ujiri to run this organization, fire Jason Kidd within weeks after bringing in Masai Ujiri. Throughout the onset of the process, it was John Scheyer and Dusty May as the top two targets for the Dallas Mavericks. That's who they really zoned in on. A group of assistants were interviewed as well, but they landed on Dusty May. A lot of executives around the NBA believe that Dusty May has been destined to make the jump. He was motivated, he wanted to do it, and that's what comes through these opportunities. You need both sides, the coach and the team, ready to make this jump.

quotes.speaker: Yaxel Lendeborg
quotes.summary_phrase: Yaxel Lendeborg on Dusty May's hiring and potential reunion
quotes.excerpt: I'm going to tell him he better pick me up. If he doesn't, I'm going to be mad.
quotes.quote: I'm going to tell him he better pick me up. If he doesn't, I'm going to be mad, I might block him. But it would be amazing being able to stick with him. I know me, Morez Johnson Jr., and Aday Mara, we talked about it, we're all going to be happy going to Dallas. If we all get an opportunity to play there, it would be awesome. Maybe he can snag Roddy and Morez as well, just have a whole Michigan starting lineup again.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Legler identifies shooting as Dallas's biggest roster weakness
quotes.excerpt: The number one thing they need is shooting. They were just anemic.
quotes.quote: The number one thing they need is shooting. They were just anemic. When you talk about modern NBA basketball, you can't make 11 threes a night and expect to really compete. 29th in makes, bottom five in attempts and percentage. For me, that's the most glaring weakness on the roster. I think you could also use some size at the power forward position. So those Michigan guys, they might come into play with that ninth pick. We'll see where he wants to go with that, but I think shooting for me has to be it. Cooper Flagg is a dynamic playmaker, you expect to get Kyrie Irving back, you need guys off the ball that can space the floor to give them more opportunities to work.

quotes.speaker: Jay Bilas
quotes.summary_phrase: Jay Bilas evaluates Dusty May's transition to the NBA
quotes.excerpt: I think it's going to be a little bit of a learning curve for him.
quotes.quote: I think it's interesting. In 96, we hired John Calipari at UMass to come to New Jersey. A lot different, we didn't have Cooper Flagg on our roster here, he does here. I think it's going to be a little bit of a learning curve for him, 82 games versus 35 to 40, but I think this is a coup for Dallas here. I think his demeanor will fit with this roster, and when you talk to the Michigan players, they'll all love to play for him, and I think it's going to be the same in Dallas.

quotes.speaker: Jay Bilas
quotes.summary_phrase: Jay Bilas on Dusty May's coaching style and leadership
quotes.excerpt: He's not like one of these yellers and screamers. He brings everybody in.
quotes.quote: Dusty May is from Indiana, and he went to IU, and he was a manager for Bob Knight. So think about that journey. One of his jobs for Coach Knight was on road trips, he'd have to get him no-yeast donuts and orange juice and leave it at his door. Then he goes to FAU as the head coach, takes them to the Final Four where he rode his bike to work every day, wins a national championship at Michigan, but he's not like one of these yellers and screamers. He brings everybody in. One of the things that he does in practice is he wants the guys to make mistakes in practice in a safe environment, feels like they learn better that way. So I think the way he deals with people and brings everybody on board is really key. He's not just a coach, he's a leader.

quotes.speaker: Malika Andrews
quotes.summary_phrase: Malika Andrews on Dusty May's impact on Elliot Cadeau
quotes.excerpt: He maximized that group. I know going to the NBA is going to be an adjustment.
quotes.quote: It showed also in how he led Elliot Cadeau and how much more confidence Elliot Cadeau played at Michigan than he did at North Carolina. To me, he maximized that group. I know going to the NBA is going to be an adjustment, but watching him at Michigan get the new players and the transfers to mesh with the returners and get them to play an unselfish brand of basketball, we can expect that same thing in Dallas.

quotes.speaker: Jay Bilas
quotes.summary_phrase: Jay Bilas on Aday Mara's development under Dusty May
quotes.excerpt: Aday Mara was at UCLA, is from Spain, but he was at UCLA and didn't play much.
quotes.quote: Aday Mara was at UCLA, is from Spain, but he was at UCLA and didn't play much. And that was a tough environment, there was a lot of tough love there. And Dusty led with love first, I think, and it allowed Mara to grow and make some mistakes. Like every Mara is a great passer, every once in a while he throw one behind the back and he wasn't, he wasn't crushed for it. I mean he's talked to about it, but I think that's a, that's a huge factor. And look, this stinks for Michigan because of the timing. You know, on June 20, 22nd, they're looking for a coach and they, you know, sign Mike Boynton as an interim coach, but that means their entire roster can walk out the door in five days if they want to. So this is difficult for Michigan, but great for Dallas and great for Dusty.
